units.source_text: 光源氏逝世之后，他的许多子孙竟难得有人承继这光辉。

en.t: After Hikaru Genji passed away, among his many descendants there were surprisingly few who inherited that brilliance.

units.source_text: 如果把退位的冷泉院也算在内，未免亵渎了他。

en.t: If one were to include the retired Reizei-in as well, it would almost be an affront to him.

units.source_text: 今上所生三皇子和同在六条院长大的薰君，此二人各有美男子之称，相貌果然长得不凡。

en.t: The Third Prince born to the reigning emperor and Lord Kaoru, who had likewise grown up at Rokujo-in, were both known as handsome men, and their looks were indeed exceptional.

units.source_text: 然而总不像源氏那样光彩焕发，令人眩目。

en.t: Yet neither of them shone with the dazzling radiance that Genji had possessed.

units.source_text: 只是比较起寻常人来，此二人生来就端正、高尚而优雅，加之血统都很尊贵；

en.t: Compared with ordinary people, however, the two were born upright, noble, and elegant, and both came from exalted bloodlines;

units.source_text: 因此世人无不敬仰，其声誉反比源氏幼时为盛。

en.t: therefore everyone in the world admired them, and their reputations were even greater than Genji's had been in his youth.

units.source_text: 这就使得两人越发得势了。

en.t: This made the two of them all the more influential.

units.source_text: 三皇子是紫夫人用心抚育长大的，故仍在夫人故居二条院内居住。

en.t: The Third Prince had been carefully brought up by Lady Murasaki, and so he still lived at Nijo-in, her former residence.

units.source_text: 大皇子是太子，身份特别高贵，今上及明石皇后对他自然另眼看待。

en.t: The First Prince was the Crown Prince, with an especially exalted rank, so the emperor and Empress Akashi naturally treated him with special regard.

units.source_text: 此外诸皇子之中，今上及皇后特别宠爱这位三皇子，希望他住在宫中，

en.t: Among the other princes, the emperor and empress especially loved this Third Prince and hoped he would live in the palace,

units.source_text: 但三皇子喜爱旧居，仍住在二条院。

en.t: but the Third Prince loved his old home and continued to live at Nijo-in.

units.source_text: 行过冠礼之后，人称他为匂兵部卿亲王。

en.t: After his coming-of-age ceremony, people called him Prince Niou, the Minister of War.

units.source_text: 大公主住在紫夫人六条院故居东南院的东殿内，一切布置装饰都照旧，毫不改变。

en.t: The Eldest Princess lived in the east wing of the southeast quarter of Rokujo-in, Lady Murasaki's former residence, where all the furnishings and decorations were kept exactly as they had been, unchanged.

units.source_text: 她在这里，朝夕想念已故的外祖母。

en.t: There, morning and evening, she thought longingly of her late grandmother.

units.source_text: 二皇子住在宫中梅壶院，娶得夕雾右大臣的二女公子为夫人，

en.t: The Second Prince lived in the Plum Court within the palace and had taken the second daughter of Minister of the Right Yugiri as his wife,

units.source_text: 时时退出宫廷，以六条院东南院的正殿作休息之所在。

en.t: and from time to time he withdrew from court and used the main hall of the southeast quarter of Rokujo-in as a place of rest.

units.source_text: 这位二皇子是将来大皇子即位后的候补太子，世间声望隆重，人品亦甚端庄。

en.t: This Second Prince was the prospective crown prince for the time after the First Prince's future accession; he enjoyed great esteem in society, and his character was also very dignified.

units.source_text: 夕雾右大臣有许多女儿，大女公子已经当了太子妃，无人竞争，独占宠爱。

en.t: Minister of the Right Yugiri had many daughters; his eldest daughter had already become the Crown Prince's consort, and with no rival she held his affection all to herself.

units.source_text: 世人都预料他们将顺次配对，明石皇后也曾如此说过。

en.t: People expected that the others would be paired off in order, and Empress Akashi had once said the same.

units.source_text: 但匂皇子不以为然，他认为婚姻之事，若非本人真心相爱，终是不放心的。

en.t: But Prince Niou did not agree; he believed that in marriage, unless the people themselves truly loved each other, one could never feel at ease.

units.source_text: 夕雾右大臣也认为：何必定要顺次配对呢？

en.t: Minister of the Right Yugiri also thought: why must they necessarily be matched in order?

units.source_text: 因此并不赞成将三女公子配给三皇子。

en.t: For that reason he did not favor giving his third daughter to the Third Prince.

units.source_text: 但倘三皇子提出求婚，则亦不必坚拒。

en.t: Still, if the Third Prince were to propose marriage, there would be no need to refuse him firmly.

units.source_text: 他非常爱护他的女儿。

en.t: He cherished his daughters very deeply.

units.source_text: 他家六女公子，是当时略有声望而自命不凡的诸亲王及公卿所追求的目标。

en.t: The sixth daughter of his house was the object pursued by princes and courtiers who had some reputation at the time and thought highly of themselves.
